P.text: An attacker places orders with very short expiration times (e.g., 1 second) at competitive prices around the spot price, with order placement being free and expired orders fully refunded without fees.
P.evidence_quote: The attacker places orders at competitive prices with `cancelTimestamp = block.timestamp + 1`, flooding the order book with orders strategically placed around the spot price

I.text: POST_ONLY orders should guarantee the user is a maker and pays lower maker fees, and legitimate POST_ONLY orders should not be blocked by expiring orders.
I.evidence_quote: The `POST_ONLY` order type is specifically designed to guarantee that the user will be a **maker** (not a taker), ensuring they pay the lower maker fees

V.text: Victims' POST_ONLY orders are rejected because expiring orders set best bid/ask prices, forcing victims to use GTC orders that become takers and pay higher taker fees (0.05% vs 0.03%).
V.evidence_quote: When victims try to place `POST_ONLY` orders at the same price, they are rejected because `getBestAskPrice() <= newOrder.price` or `getBestBidPrice() >= newOrder.price`
